main.t: One of a pair of curved bones forming most of the upper sides and top of the skull (parietal bone).

simpler.t: The parietal bones form the top and sides of your head.

deeper.t: The two parietal bones meet along the top of the skull at the sagittal suture.

facts.t: It forms most of the upper side of the skull; the right and left meet at the top.
The frontal bone is in front, the temporal bone below and the occipital bone behind.
It is one of the flat bones that form the top and sides of the brain case.

simpler.t: It forms most of the top and side of your head.

deeper.t: The parietal is one of the four bones that meet at the pterion, the weakest part of the skull.

items.name: Sagittal border
items.t: Meets the other parietal bone at the sagittal suture.

items.name: Frontal border
items.t: Meets the frontal bone at the coronal suture.

items.name: Occipital border
items.t: Meets the occipital bone at the lambdoid suture.

items.name: Squamous border
items.t: Meets the squamous part of the temporal bone at the squamous suture.

items.name: Grooves on the inner surface
items.t: Branches of the artery that supplies the brain’s coverings mark the inner surface of the skull.
items.check: OpenStax says the artery’s branches groove the inner surface of the skull; that this includes the parietal bone needs an approved source.

simpler.t: It is a curved plate of bone, joined to its neighbours by sutures.

deeper.t: Its sutures twist tightly, interlocking it with its neighbours to strengthen the skull.

facts.t: As a curved flat bone of the brain case, it encloses and protects the brain.
Its twisting sutures interlock with the neighbouring bones, adding strength.
Sutures are fibrous joints that allow almost no movement.

simpler.t: It is a strong, curved shield over the brain.

items.name: Sagittal suture
items.t: Unites the right and left parietal bones along the midline.

items.name: Coronal suture
items.t: Joins it to the frontal bone.

items.name: Lambdoid suture
items.t: Joins it to the occipital bone.

items.name: Squamous suture
items.t: Joins it to the temporal bone.

items.name: Superior sagittal sinus
items.t: A large vein of the brain’s coverings, running in the midline beneath the top of the skull.

simpler.t: Sutures join it to the frontal, occipital and temporal bones, and to its partner.

facts.t: It forms directly from membrane (intramembranous ossification), like the other bones of the top and sides of the brain case.
In a baby, wide areas of connective tissue (fontanelles) separate it from its neighbours.
The fontanelles narrow greatly during the first year, as the bones enlarge, and become sutures.

items.injury: The sagittal suture closes too early (craniosynostosis).
items.damaged: The joint between the two parietal bones fuses.
items.cannotDo: Grow across the top of the head: the head becomes long and narrow (scaphocephaly).
items.why: Growth is diverted to the sides of the skull, which grow upwards.

items.injury: A blow to the side of the head.
items.damaged: A linear fracture, with lines radiating from the point of impact.
items.cannotDo: Escape the risk of bleeding inside the skull, which can injure the brain.
items.why: A fracture of the brain case can tear the vessels inside it.

items.q: Explain why a newborn’s skull can change shape during birth.
model: The brain case bones are still separated by wide fontanelles.
These are areas of dense connective tissue.
They let the bones push closer together or overlap slightly.
So the head can pass through the birth canal.

items.q: Compare a suture with a fontanelle.
model: Both are fibrous joints between skull bones.
A fontanelle is a wide area of connective tissue in a baby’s skull.
A suture is a narrow, convoluted fibrous joint in the adult skull.
Fontanelles narrow into sutures as the bones grow.

items.q: Predict the head shape if the sagittal suture fuses too early, and explain it.
model: The skull cannot widen across the top.
Growth is diverted to the sides, which grow upwards.
The head becomes long, narrow and wedge-shaped (scaphocephaly).
The brain still has room to grow normally.

check.stem: Which suture joins the two parietal bones?
check.why: The sagittal suture unites the right and left parietal bones.

check.stem: How do the parietal bones develop?
check.why: The bones of the top and sides of the brain case form directly from membrane.

options: A fracture of the parietal bone
A long, narrow head from early fusion of the sagittal suture
check.why: Early closure of the sagittal suture diverts growth upwards at the sides.
